rows.en: Fores: "...Excellency. About the Spirit Mechs...
Are you really sure we can leave them alone?
I hear even Rayblade has activated.
Isn't it dangerous?"
Growster: "Hmph. Exaggerated legends have merely
glorified those things. The course of a war isn't something
a single Armored Mech can change.
What matters is the quality and spirit of the soldier piloting it.
The same applies to Spirit Mechs."
Fores: "Understood..."
Growster: "...What's wrong?
That isn't all you came to say, is it?"
Fores: "Yes, sir... Why did you entrust the vanguard to Captain Falmore?
I'd like to understand your true intention.
I don't mean to insult a fellow soldier,
but he'll use any means to achieve his goal.
He's capable, but there's a danger
of never knowing what he'll do."
Growster: "I've heard about him too.
Including his near-blackmail over Grad's
return to the army. But a man like that has his uses.
You can't run a country or an army on pretty ideals alone."
Fores: "I understand that, but..."
Growster: "Don't worry. That's precisely why I'm assigning
your favorite, Lieutenant Dalaim, to him."
Fores: "What?! Wh-Who would want that..."
Growster: "Ha ha ha! Don't be embarrassed.
I don't distinguish between men and women as soldiers,
but marrying and bearing children is a privilege only women have.
It's about time you..."
Fores: "Excellency!"
Growster: "Don't be so angry. I didn't say
you should retire."
Fores: "I know! And I..."
Growster: "You aren't entirely against him, are you?"
Fores: "Excellency?!"
Growster: "Gah ha ha ha!
...Anyway, we simply fulfill our duty as soldiers
and obey our country's decisions.
For once, we should thank that daytime lantern.
I can finally settle things with Revios.
It's that daytime lantern's fault it took this long.
Hmm. His dawdling is why Agarthia's
people look down on us!"
Fores: (Th-This turn of events... His Excellency's complaints...)
Growster: "And now that man is off relaxing
at a villa at a time like this... Just what does he think he's doing
as head of state?!"
Fores: (...I knew it...)
Growster: "It was a huge mistake to appoint someone
who only got into politics through his parents' influence
president and head of state. Welfare, charity...
He does nothing but chase popularity. And then,
once elected, what was the very first thing he did?
Build that villa! Whatever pretext he uses,
all he's doing is using public money
for his own whims! Election promises turn into mere lip service,
and he only makes the smallest token effort.
It's always been that way, but he's especially awful.
Compared to him, all those previous imbeciles
were far better.
He's the only one who naps in his office!
Politicians think only of their own interests,
cozying up to contractors, rotten with corruption.
The president shamelessly wastes public funds on himself.
What is going to happen to this country?!
You agree, don't you?! Well?!"
Fores: "...Y-Yes, sir. I agree..."
Growster: "No, you don't understand yet.
I'll explain it to you at length today.
Come on, sit down there."
Fores: "N-No, I... Oh."
Growster: "Now, where had I got to?
Oh, yes. We were discussing this country's future.
To begin with..."
Growster: "Hmm? What is it at a time like this...? Come in!"
Fores: (I-I'm saved...)
Reamond: "...Excuse me. Oh, Lieutenant Colonel."
Fores: "Lieutenant..."
Reamond: 'Is it happening "again"?'
Fores: 'If you were coming, why couldn't you come sooner?!'
Reamond: 'What am I supposed to say to that...?'
Growster: "Hmm? What are you whispering about?"
Fores: "N-Nothing!"
Growster: "Well, never mind.
Have you finished preparing to move out?"
Reamond: "Yes."
Fores: "That doesn't mean you have nothing to do, does it?"
Reamond: "Don't be so cold...
Coming to see you..."
Fores: "..."
Reamond: "H-Ha ha ha... If you look so frightening,
that lovely face will... H-Huh?
Why are you clenching your fists...?"
Fores: "Stop saying stupid things and go get ready!
Excellency, I'll take my leave!"
Growster: "Hmm?"
Reamond: "Ow... Oh? Lieutenant Colonel, where are you going?"
Fores: "Wh-Wherever I please!"
Reamond: "Oh! I see. The bathroom."
Fores: "...!"
Reamond: "Whoa!"
Reamond: "That isn't funny..."
Fores: "Hmph!"
Growster: "You two get along as well as ever."
Reamond: "That's her way of showing affection, Lieutenant Colonel style."
Growster: "I doubt it, but never mind.
How did it go?"
Reamond: "Yes. There were even cameras.
No wonder they could anticipate our movements.
I tampered with all of them, though."
Growster: "I thought so. Just what that daytime lantern would do."
Reamond: "But why would the president do such a thing?"
Growster: "He trusts no one.
Except himself. Too many fools can't see through him!
But just you wait. I'll tear off
that mask of his! And another thing..."
Reamond: "Th-Then I'll be going!"
Growster: "........"
Baio: "...Pardon me."
Growster: "...Baio. I won't buy any Armored Mechs."
Baio: "I haven't even spoken yet."
Growster: "Am I mistaken?"
Baio: "Grrr... Well, yes. Today I've come
to sell my life's greatest masterpiece.
Why won't you use my Bine Daga?!
It's second to no Armored Mech!
No, no Spirit Mech either! No..."
Growster: "Yes, yes, I understand.
But a mech that chooses its pilot like that
is worthless as a weapon.
A mech that needs special training is more troublesome than a Spirit Mech.
And what's with that price? For the cost of one,
how many Armored Mechs could we build?"
Baio: "What of it? It's your obsession with trivialities
that makes Agarthia look down on you.
Choose Bine Daga and those worries are solved at once.
As a special offer, I'll throw in a Bine Daga maintenance kit!"
Growster: "I told you I don't need it."
Baio: "Grrr... W-Well, as a special exception,
for up to ten installments,
I'll make Bio pay the installment fees."
Growster: "That isn't what I'm talking about.
If you're so insistent, I might consider that Daga you brought,
though."
Baio: "Daga? Well, it's not a bad mech,
but you could take Bine Daga along with it..."
Growster: "No, no.
Will you sell Daga or won't you? Which?"
Baio: "...Much obliged..."
Growster: "...What a stubborn man."
Growster: "...Still, that Bio.
He said, 'Profit doesn't always mean money.'
Is that what this is...?
Honestly... What does he enjoy
about troubling his own brother...?"
Horem: "...Then let's begin preparations
to transfer the data."
Cain: "If he knew this project was running again,
what would General Growster think?"
Horem: "Heh heh... By the time he realizes,
he'll be another of my puppets."
Cain: "...You're a scary man."
Horem: "Am I? I'm just being honest with myself.
I thought the same was true of you."
Cain: "Well, we're alike that way.
This should be interesting.
York was over surprisingly quickly."
Horem: "Growster's much-vaunted Armored Mechs
must have been quite effective. I regret that
the summoning device couldn't be used.
Who expected a link to the Holy Land...?
And we've failed to get our hands on a Spirit Mech.
Still, obtaining data and resources
will have to do."
Cain: "Spirit Mechs? Hmph. I saw a little of them. They're hopeless.
Complete amateurs at fighting."
Horem: "Aren't you an amateur too?"
Cain: "...Are you trying to anger me?"
Horem: "Not at all. Was that a slip of the tongue?
I merely meant I wouldn't recommend
underestimating their power."
Cain: "You think I could lose to those fools?"
Horem: "No, no. Of course not.
Oh, speaking of which, I hear Liebhofen
has entered our territory.
Apparently they're heading for those research-facility ruins.
Nothing to do with you, of course."
Cain: "...Hmph. Very well.
If you insist, I'll show you my power. Plenty of it."
Horem: "Really? That would help.
We can't let them investigate that place yet."
Cain: "Well, just sit there and watch..."
Horem: "..."
Horem: "...Perhaps I'd better take out a little insurance..."
Horem: "...Oh, excuse me, but could I ask you
to take on a job?"
????: "That's outside our contract."
Horem: "Naturally, I'll pay you.
Your opponents this time are Spirit Mechs.
It should be a good opportunity to collect data."
????: "...Very well. Explain the details."
Horem: "Just what I'd expect of Vales Briar.
I'm glad we can settle this quickly."
Vales: "Spare me the flattery. Get to the point."
Horem: "My apologies. Now, then..."
